work.title: The Tragedy of Antony and Cleopatra
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. A plain in Syria.

content.text: Enter Ventidius as it were in triumph, with Silius and other Romans, Officers and Soldiers; the dead body of Pacorus borne before him.

lines.text: Now, darting Parthia, art thou struck, and now
lines.plainText: Now darting Parthia art thou struck and now

lines.text: Pleased Fortune does of Marcus Crassus' death
lines.plainText: Pleased Fortune does of Marcus Crassus' death

lines.text: Make me revenger. Bear the king's son's body
lines.plainText: Make me revenger Bear the king's son's body

lines.text: Before our army. Thy Pacorus, Orodes,
lines.plainText: Before our army Thy Pacorus Orodes

lines.text: Pays this for Marcus Crassus.
lines.plainText: Pays this for Marcus Crassus

lines.text: Noble Ventidius,
lines.plainText: Noble Ventidius

lines.text: Whilst yet with Parthian blood thy sword is warm,
lines.plainText: Whilst yet with Parthian blood thy sword is warm

lines.text: The fugitive Parthians follow. Spur through Media,
lines.plainText: The fugitive Parthians follow Spur through Media

lines.text: Mesopotamia, and the shelters whither
lines.plainText: Mesopotamia and the shelters whither

lines.text: The routed fly. So thy grand captain Antony
lines.plainText: The routed fly So thy grand captain Antony

lines.text: Shall set thee on triumphant chariots, and
lines.plainText: Shall set thee on triumphant chariots and

lines.text: Put garlands on thy head.
lines.plainText: Put garlands on thy head

lines.text: O Silius, Silius,
lines.plainText: O Silius Silius

lines.text: I have done enough. A lower place, note well,
lines.plainText: I have done enough A lower place note well

lines.text: May make too great an act. For learn this, Silius:
lines.plainText: May make too great an act For learn this Silius

lines.text: Better to leave undone than by our deed
lines.plainText: Better to leave undone than by our deed

lines.text: Acquire too high a fame when him we serve's away.
lines.plainText: Acquire too high a fame when him we serve's away

lines.text: Caesar and Antony have ever won
lines.plainText: Caesar and Antony have ever won

lines.text: More in their officer, than person. Sossius,
lines.plainText: More in their officer than person Sossius

lines.text: One of my place in Syria, his lieutenant,
lines.plainText: One of my place in Syria his lieutenant

lines.text: For quick accumulation of renown,
lines.plainText: For quick accumulation of renown

lines.text: Which he achieved by th' minute, lost his favour.
lines.plainText: Which he achieved by th' minute lost his favour

lines.text: Who does i' th' wars more than his captain can
lines.plainText: Who does i' th' wars more than his captain can

lines.text: Becomes his captain's captain; and ambition,
lines.plainText: Becomes his captain's captain and ambition

lines.text: The soldier's virtue, rather makes choice of loss
lines.plainText: The soldier's virtue rather makes choice of loss

lines.text: Than gain which darkens him.
lines.plainText: Than gain which darkens him

lines.text: I could do more to do Antonius good,
lines.plainText: I could do more to do Antonius good

lines.text: But 'twould offend him, and in his offence
lines.plainText: But 'twould offend him and in his offence

lines.text: Should my performance perish.
lines.plainText: Should my performance perish

lines.text: Thou hast, Ventidius, that
lines.plainText: Thou hast Ventidius that

lines.text: Without the which a soldier and his sword
lines.plainText: Without the which a soldier and his sword

lines.text: Grants scarce distinction. Thou wilt write to Antony?
lines.plainText: Grants scarce distinction Thou wilt write to Antony

lines.text: I'll humbly signify what in his name,
lines.plainText: I'll humbly signify what in his name

lines.text: That magical word of war, we have effected;
lines.plainText: That magical word of war we have effected

lines.text: How, with his banners, and his well-paid ranks,
lines.plainText: How with his banners and his wellpaid ranks

lines.text: The ne'er-yet-beaten horse of Parthia
lines.plainText: The ne'eryetbeaten horse of Parthia

lines.text: We have jaded out o' th' field.
lines.plainText: We have jaded out o' th' field

lines.text: Where is he now?
lines.plainText: Where is he now

lines.text: He purposeth to Athens, whither, with what haste
lines.plainText: He purposeth to Athens whither with what haste

lines.text: The weight we must convey with 's will permit,
lines.plainText: The weight we must convey with 's will permit

lines.text: We shall appear before him.—On there, pass along!
